comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose revenue declines in their server-related segments in 2024, citing customer inventory normalization and lower demand as primary drivers. Intel's DCAI revenue decreased $4.2 billion, with server volume dropping 37% due to a softening CPU data center market. Similarly, AMD's Embedded segment revenue decreased by 33% primarily because 'customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.' While Intel focuses on the volume decline in the general server/CPU market, AMD highlights inventory normalization in its Embedded segment, reflecting similar downstream demand pressures in the server/data center infrastructure ecosystem.

sentences.text: ▪DCAI revenue decreased $4.2 billion from 2022, driven by a decrease in server revenue. Server volume decreased 37% from 2022, due to lower demand in a softening CPU data center market. Server ASPs increased 20% from 2022, primarily due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer-related revenue and a higher mix of high core count products.
Embedded net revenue of $3.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.

comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom analyze server/data center revenue drivers in their 2024 Item 7 disclosures, but they report opposite trends. Intel reports a significant decrease in Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenue driven by a 37% drop in server volume due to a softening CPU data center market. In contrast, Broadcom reports an increase in its Semiconductor Solutions segment revenue (which includes server storage) driven by strong demand for AI networking products, although this was partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage products. Intel's decline is attributed to volume contraction in the CPU market, while Broadcom's growth is linked to AI networking demand.
